Corporations are required to do this by law if they want to protect their trademarks (brandnames). Trademark law requires them to actively pursue infringing uses of their trademark or the trademark becomes null and void.

Now, this doesn't mean they have to sue every infringing use into oblivion. If they find a mom and pop shop using a similar name they can come to an agreement where the mom and pop shop recognizes the corporate ownership of said trademark and enter into some form of usage agreement (thus strengthening the trademark claim). Unfortunately this rarely happens (probably because it takes more effort and isn't quite as iron clad as just shutting them down completely).

The OP mentioned case wasn't trademark/brandname based though. It was copyright infringement which is entirely different can of worms (and even more dubious).

No. Most modern democracies in developed nations use some form of proportional representation. In our system if you get 8% of the vote then you get 100% of the representation so long as the second highest guy got 7%. It's pretty silly and means smaller parties like green, libertarian, etc stand almost no chance of getting somebody into high office. On the other hand imagine we simply setup representatives as 100 seats and if you get at least 1% of the vote then you are guaranteed at least one seat. Suddenly every single esoteric interest is going to be able to get some representation and this is a great thing since it helps keep the political system of checks and balances functioning.

The judiciary is going to be reflective of the political system as a whole. And in our country the entire political system is pay to win.
